status: independent partner-agency witness, exploratory check, not the registered test
title: A second witness from the ground: station-based rainfall from KNMI Climate Explorer

witness.name: KNMI Climate Explorer (Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute)
witness.dataset: CRU TS 4.10 precipitation (pre), 0.5 degree, land points, 1901-2025
witness.dataset_authors: Harris et al. 2020; University of East Anglia Climatic Research Unit (CRU)
witness.how_made: Climate Explorer 'Monthly observations' > Precipitation > CRU TS 4.10 (land) 0.5 deg, 'Make average' over lat 10-18N, lon 17W-25E, land points only (more than 50 percent land from the CRU land/sea mask, at least 30 percent valid points), monthly series left in mm/month; JJAS mean computed here as the sum of the four months divided by their days
witness.citation: KNMI Climate Explorer, Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute; data: CRU TS 4.10, Harris et al. 2020 / University of East Anglia CRU
witness.kind: station-based gridded analysis (rain gauges interpolated to 0.5 degree), independent of satellites and reanalysis

case.claim_text: Wet-season rainfall over the central Sahel has increased

levels.note: IMERG level is the regional anomaly plus the registered baseline mean from the bundle (cell anomalies, cos-latitude weighted, ocean cells included in the box); CRU is land points only, so the levels are not expected to match and only the year-to-year behaviour and the trend are compared.

knmi_cru.sen_ci_method: analytic Sen interval (Gilbert) with Hamed-Rao variance, same routine as the registered test

our_imerg.sen_ci_method: analytic Sen interval (Gilbert) with Hamed-Rao variance, same routine as the registered test

difference_knmi_minus_imerg.sen_ci_method: analytic Sen interval (Gilbert) with Hamed-Rao variance, same routine as the registered test

registered_reference.note: Copied read-only from the registered case bundle. Nothing in this file changes it.
registered_reference.interval_method: residual moving-block bootstrap around the Sen line, percentile 95%

caveat: CRU TS is built from rain-gauge stations, so it does not depend on satellites or on a reanalysis model, but it has its own limits: stations are sparse across the Sahel and counts have changed over time, so where there are few gauges the grid leans on the long-term average and on distant stations. It also covers land only, while our box includes some ocean. Treat it as a cross-check on direction and year-to-year behaviour, not as ground truth.
scope_note: exploratory check, not the registered test. The registered result is the trend test in the case bundle; nothing here replaces it.
